Open `Inference_Examples.qmd` in the prepared Posit Cloud project and select
**Render** to create `Inference_Examples.pdf`.
Use `|>` to pass a dataset into an `eco230r` test. Change the variables and
explain the results in context when practicing with your own data.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(eco230r)
data("tea_tab", package = "eco230r")
data("t_tall", package = "eco230r")
data("t_wide", package = "eco230r")
data("napData", package = "eco230r")
```

## Week 7: Chi-square tests

The tea examples match the interpretation slides. Goodness of fit compares one
categorical variable to expected proportions; independence examines two
categorical variables. The default goodness-of-fit model uses equal proportions.

```{r}
tea_fit <- tea_tab |> csf(~ cool_time)
tea_fit$results
tea_fit$standardized_residuals

tea_association <- tea_tab |> csi(finger_preference ~ cool_time)
tea_association$results
tea_association$standardized_residuals
```

## Week 8: t-tests and Wilcoxon tests

Use two groups for independent samples, paired measurements from the same units
for paired tests, and a stated reference value for a one-sample test.

```{r}
independent <- t_tall |> idt(scones ~ tea)
independent$results

paired <- t_wide |> pst(black_tea ~ green_tea)
paired$results

one_sample <- t_tall |> ost(~ scones, mu = 45)
one_sample$results

independent_ranks <- t_tall |> idw(scones ~ tea)
independent_ranks$results

paired_ranks <- t_wide |> psw(black_tea ~ green_tea)
paired_ranks$results
```

## Week 9: ANOVA and regression

ANOVA compares group means; regression estimates a relationship with a numeric
predictor. Use the effect size and uncertainty to explain practical importance.

```{r}
anova_example <- napData |> ano(naptime ~ light)
anova_example$results

regression_example <- napData |> slr(naptime ~ timestamp)
regression_example$results
```

## Interpret each analysis

1. State the story and why it matters.
2. Describe the estimates or plot and the decision they suggest.
3. Select the test and state the null and alternative hypotheses.
4. Interpret the statistical evidence against the null.
5. Explain the magnitude and practical consequence for the decision maker.
